title: Moment algebra inequality
statement: Let $R,a,b,A,D,C\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $9\le R$, $0\le a$, $0\le b$, $0\le C$, $0\le D$, $A\le Ra^2$, $D\le b^2$, and $C^2\le AD$. Then $A+6C+RD\le R(a+b)^2$.
hypotheses_covered: R, a, b, A, D, and C are real
replaced: Let $R,a,b,A,D,C\in\bbr$ satisfy $R\ge9$, $a,b,C,D\ge0$, $A\le Ra^2$, $D\le b^2$, and $C^2\le AD$. Then $A+6C+RD\le R(a+b)^2$.
